title: The Seven Spirits and the Rejection of the Covenant
english: A man was seen to have come through lowliness and a despised nature. But the judgment interpreted according to the law—neither for this present age nor for the coming one—is not to be forgiven. For when the law commands the condemned God to die, and the Lord is held against the law, [it does] not grant forgiveness for such a thing.

But if the forgiveness through baptism is kept silent in such matters, since there was not even a time to discourse with the Jews about this; for there is found a certain distinction between the [judgment] in this age and the coming one, that the one being baptized will be from this age; and a certain distinction is examined between the present and the coming life, and thus it holds a denial of the examination from the law, according to Paul the speaker saying, 'God is the one who justifies; who is the one who condemns?' (Romans 8:33). Does not the doing of wonders and the loosening of demons, which only the Spirit does, leaving these things to the demon, leave you no forgiveness for the blasphemy? He says this, not refusing that the blasphemy against himself be forgiven, nor [refusing] a place of repentance for those blaspheming against the Spirit, if they wished, but claiming that the blasphemy against him, as against a man, would then only seem to be a lesser thing when compared to the blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, but after the resurrection from the dead and the ascent to heaven and it being clearly shown that he is truly the Son of God and God. Even if he has become unchangeably a man, the blasphemy against him will not be forgiven, unless through a sincere repentance of his fault.

From this we learn (Mt 12:43-45) that a demon will not overpower a man of better disposition, but such a one will be an impassable barrier to him, having virtue preceding, and leaving no place for him, as the Preacher advises. On the contrary, the evil and reckless man is a rider for the evil spirit regarding the good. And we learn that the demons also possess a certain consolation for those who are suitable to themselves; for when they are not able to do this, they do not rest, just as it is said from the opposites that the rest of the Divine Spirit is the suitability toward men; for 'the Holy [One] rests in the holy [ones]' (Ps 99:2).

God. But the entering in with many after the one-time departure has a cause in the unchangeable wickedness of man. And the seven spirits are to be considered much; for among the multitudes, many times the seven are [mentioned] according to the divine Scripture. In the beginning, indeed, the evil spirit dwelt among the Jews, when in Egypt they were idolaters; but it departed when they were called by God. After these things, when it had failed against the one who was called, then the grace passed over to the Gentiles, and they were being given out. And the one among the Gentiles became a dwelling of the evil ones, both harsh and inaccessible, having received God, the Gentiles. But the return to Israel is easier than before, and with a great multitude of the exodus. Therefore, it is bad that they now pass through, being constantly arranged toward the blasphemy against Christ as in Egypt, not having the covenant toward Abraham, and not expecting according to justice even as then, but being cut off from hope, because they have rejected the fulfiller of this. Thus the Lord has made manifest in the words toward them both their remaining rejection and the judgment of the coming shame, and the already-established rule by the evil one.

That his brothers did not believe in him (Mt 12:46), we learn from John, and from Mark we have heard somewhat more: as if they were attempting to hold [him] having gone astray. With such a mind, the Lord did not remember [them] as his own, but he demonstrates the subjects; to these he foretells all the names of the relatives, who, according to the intimacy of obedience to him, were joined together. And even if Mary's opposition was only for a time, just as Simeon also foretold saying, 'and your own soul' and the following, it is fitting that the Lord also returned to these things favorably, remembering her passion and having joined her to the beloved disciple.

In these things it is sought how he did not say that the word had been sown in the beginning, nor did he say the seed beside the road was sown, but this is the one sown beside the road (Mt 13:18-23); even though after a little while he showed the seed to be existing in those in whom he says the word is being compressed and becomes unfruitful. title: The Net and the Fish
english: He shows not that it is sown into them, but they themselves. Therefore we say that the Word is both seed and that which received the word through comparison and likeness to himself. Because of this, Christ is formed in us and we are being formed according to Christ.

He likens the world to a sea because of the bitterness and the billows of trouble within it (Mt 13:47), but the power of the Word, casting a net upon the world, gathers from various thoughts of the old and new Scripture, from Greeks and barbarians, wise and foolish, men and women, free and slaves, righteous and wicked. The net is filled when the master who casts it knows; for this is not for a man to recognize. When the Word of instruction already has the measure of the fullness, then not all who have undertaken the learning of the Word will be found worthy to the master of the net, but a distinction then will occur between the wicked and the good; and to the useless, the end will appear as destruction, but to the good, the dwelling placed by the Lord into different vessels: for many are the dwellings by the Father. But the wicked, who are counted temporarily with the righteous, will no longer have with them the indistinguishable [state] through weariness, leaving behind for themselves a sweet life, just as fish in the sea; they will undergo the most painful punishment in fire, where nothing remains for the consolation of evil.

The Savior likened the world to the sea because of the trouble and confusion within it, but the power of the Word, casting a net upon the world, was being fulfilled from various thoughts of old and new [Scripture] gathered from every kind of Greeks and barbarians, wise and foolish. Of more wonders and greater events by our Savior (Mt 14:17), it is not less that there is not always use of authority for the abundance of food, but it is necessary many times to be in need and to be without (Mt 15:2).
The Lord turns the evil state of the Pharisees into opposites; for those caring for the bodily things despised the spiritual, but the Savior, introducing the spiritual, renounces the bodily.

Indeed, following the preceding demonstration, the voice of the prophet was applied at the right time, possessing much concord with it (Mt 15:8). Where did the Canaanite woman come from? (Mt 15:21-22) From the idolatry of Tyre and Sidon, from her own people, and from 'the house of her father.' Where did she come from? She came forth as a fragrance of myrrh for the Savior; for she holds a type of the Church from among the Gentiles. But also the Savior came out from the 'kinship' of Israel and from 'his own house,' which is Jerusalem. And the Canaanite woman receives him, she who also received Elijah, the widow; and what did she cry out, shouting: 'Lord, Son of David!'? How did she know to call thus, having studied neither the law nor the prophets? She called him 'Lord' according to his divinity, but 'Son of David' according to the flesh. Consider for me the widow's son who was dead, that is, the body which had been made dead, and the soul having been purified from the demon; he restored both the body and the soul.

For neither does a physician satisfy an untimely desire of those who are sick by seeking the remedy of the disease, nor the fulfillment of pleasure; nor does the Savior fulfill an irrational desire in order to show power. For it is not profitable for such people to be showered with graces which, not being sufficient, do not suffice. Moreover, they ask for a sign from heaven, such as foods like those in the days of the fathers, or a standing of the elements like in the days of Joshua. Having said that they are a wicked generation, he leaves the faithful Zion, the synagogue of the Jews, like a bridegroom leaving a city that has become a prostitute. Just as a physician does not give an untimely desire to those who are sick as a way of loosening their disease, nor does he satisfy their pleasure with harmful foods, so also the Savior does not fulfill an irrational desire to show his power; for many signs from heaven they have seen: 'a spirit descending like a dove' (Mt 16:1-4), the heavens having been opened and the paternal 'voice saying: This is my beloved Son.'

Yet he does not provide an apology to those who work the passion through these things; for the mindset and the conspiracy of the Jews did not harmonize with the counsel of God, nor did they hasten then, which God managed; so that for them, what was being done was impiety according to their opinion, but to God it was a wise dispensation and, to mankind, a saving benefit (Mt 16:23).
And that which is in the glory of his Father: he says 'the glory,' meaning the glory of God, because having become man, he is the Son of God (Mt 16:27).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Fish and the Lost Sheep
english: As it shows in parallel, having placed both as the Son of Man, saying and that he would appear in the glory of his Father. And he confirms what is being said also with his angels; for the angels are of God, and not of any creature, nor of man. Because of this, indeed, 'Lord of Powers' is a name for God. And a name of identity is a mark of knowledge. And he says that such one appearing gives to each according to his deed.

Regarding Matthew 17:5, the Father announcing the Son appears from the voice heard there, as if proclaiming and itself the testimony coming from above through all; for a voice of God is not to be considered heard [by the ear], nor is the sensible from the incorporeal. And just as 'no one has seen God ever' (John 1:18), neither has [anyone] heard God. But what you hear of his dispensation has the power of necessity; for he says [it is] rather than the prophets introduced by Moses, that the time has already advanced and to depart from the introduction toward perfection, from the types toward the truth; for the law having been introduced through the appearance from above, it was not possible for the greater to prevail among men if not introduced by the appearance from above.

Regarding Matthew 17:22-23, he therefore says that what is going to happen in Jerusalem is not yet approaching, nor the time according to which it was necessary to suffer, so that he might reveal the divine foreknowledge being such, and that he was about to suffer voluntarily, not departing from where he was to be persuaded through ignorance. And it happened for the disciples' benefit so that they would not be troubled as if men had prevailed against him.

Regarding Matthew 17:24, this was a legal matter concerning the drachmas, having been determined by Moses saying: 'each will give a ransom for his own soul, the half of a drachma' (Exodus 30:13). These things indeed the Jews were collecting from everyone, and the drachma was being given as a ransom for two souls according to the law; neither was it being added to the rich one, as the law has said, nor was it being diminished for the poor one 'from the half of a drachma'. That is, he says, the holy [thing] is according to the drachma, nothing else being hinted at regarding the matter, or the true ransom, since all things were being shadowed toward this. And the true ransom was the Lord, having the Father in himself by power, as a divine character is, of which the giving of the drachma is a symbol, even though it is a drachma...

Regarding the redemption, no one can give more than half, even if they become rich. The mystery was that the Son could not be separated from the Father, nor could one understand anything lacking of perfection concerning Christ, whence it is said, 'all the fullness of deity dwells in him bodily' (Col 2:9).

He presents himself as creator and lord of the sea and those in it and every element, as the proper Son of God and Father. For this fish held a type of the church, which of old was seized by the salt and dread of unbelief and was deeply submerged in the depth, and was baptized and tossed by the storm and surge of worldly pleasures; but it was hauled up by the hook of the apostles, through teaching and fishing and the word that hunts, toward the knowledge of God, 'who called us out of darkness into his marvelous light' (1 Pet 2:9).

Because of this, it is fitting to adapt his coming into the world to the previously set parable as if it were a sheep that has become lost; that is, the man being among the hundred sheep, from the multitude of the heavenly powers, being similar to them as a rational being, being counted as a sheep among sheep, yet being the least compared to the great multitude, and therefore one hundred among sheep. But his wandering is the stumbling of Adam. It is sought appropriately that he also remain similar to those remaining with God, and for their replenishment it is necessary, so that the shepherd might not be lacking and be a stump, just as Paul said that they might 'recapitulate all things' in Christ (Eph 1:10), the recovery of the part that had flowed away, since the standing together of the whole in Christ is not complete due to what is missing and lacking.

It is peculiar to the parable to command that the woman and children and all that she has be sold and returned; for regarding human affairs this is possible, but regarding the judgment from Christ, things not owned are not being sold, nor would the repayment of debts occur. But the taking away of all things which someone has for pleasure and for enjoyment, and the repayment through sufferings, is shown; and regarding opposites, the opposite is released; thus, labors dissolve pleasures.
